elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "Vendor may audit Customer no more than once every 12 months" — replaces the original "at any time without notice."

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: independent auditor "bound by confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2: "Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall."

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2: "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly"; the conflicting remote-access permission in original 22.1 ("may remotely access Customer's systems and records") is deleted, so no contradictory retained sentence remains.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1 caps audits at "no more than once every 12 months", which satisfies a once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1 requires "30 days' written notice", which exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2 shifts costs to Customer at an underpayment "exceeding five percent", not ten percent; read literally the fallback threshold is not present. This is the preferred-level formulation, so the preferred checklist is nonetheless complete and no repair is needed.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; noted only for completeness — 22.2 bars direct system access and the walk-away remote-access language is removed.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single replacement of Section 22.1 supplies frequency (once per 12 months), 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where possible, and an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, while the already-protective cost-allocation (5%) and no-direct-system-access language in Section 22.2 is left intact.

The walk-away features of the original clause (unlimited, unannounced audits and remote access to Customer systems) are eliminated, and the deletion also cures the internal conflict with the no-direct-access sentence in 22.2.

Minimal: one surgical replacement of the offending sentence, no survival tails, procedures, expense allocations, remedies or other extras added, and no Customer-favourable retained language removed. Section 22.2 is untouched, so there is no duplicate cost or access mechanic.
Preserves intent: Vendor retains a usage-audit right and the shortfall/cost-reimbursement mechanic; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.
The fallback cost element (10% threshold) is not literally present because the contract uses the preferred 5% trigger; this requires no repair since the preferred checklist is fully met.
Severity remains medium; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the original 22.1 failed even the fallback (no frequency cap, no notice) and reached walk-away territory.
